summary: Put it on a label, type a key, and the text follows the current language forever after.
overview: The component you actually use. Everything else in the folder exists to feed this one. Add it beside a TextMeshPro label, type a key, and that label shows the key's text in the current language and rewrites itself the moment the language changes — no code, no manual refresh, nothing to subscribe to.
useCases: Every piece of fixed UI text in the game: menu items, button labels, headings, tooltips.
A line with a value in it — "You have {0} coins" — where the value comes from the game and the wording comes from the language.
One reusable status label that shows different lines at different times, via SetKey.

params.why: REQUIRED. The lookup key, e.g. "menu.start". The same key exists in every language — that is what makes switching work.
params.tuning: Leave it EMPTY and the component does nothing at all: the label keeps whatever text it was authored with, no warning. That is deliberate, so a half-built screen is not covered in markers, but it also means a forgotten key looks exactly like a working one. The inspector's Pick Key button lists the keys that really exist, and previews the text in every language underneath.

params.why: The TextMeshPro label to write into.
params.tuning: Optional. Left empty, the component looks for a TMP_Text on ITS OWN GameObject — not on children. On a Button, that means this component belongs on the Label child, not on the Button.

params.why: A legacy UnityEngine.UI.Text target, for a project not on TextMeshPro.
params.tuning: Optional, and only used when there is no TMP target. Auto-found the same way. If neither exists on the GameObject you get one console warning naming the object, rather than silence.

params.why: Apply the active language's Font Override to this label, if it has one.
params.tuning: On by default, which is what you want for body text. Turn it OFF for a label whose font is deliberately fixed — a logo, a stylised title — so a CJK font swap does not flatten it.

usage.codeNote: The key's text in that language must contain {0}, {1} and so on for the arguments to land anywhere. If a translator breaks the placeholders, the raw template is shown and the key is named in the console.

apiNotes.SetArguments(params object[]): Stored, not applied once. That is the difference that matters: a formatted label survives a language switch without the caller doing anything, because Refresh re-formats from the stored values every time.
apiNotes.SetKey(string): Swaps which line this label shows and refreshes immediately. Useful for one reusable status or prompt label.
apiNotes.Refresh(): Re-reads the current language. Called for you on enable and on every language change; you only need it after changing something the component cannot see.
apiNotes.Key: Read-only. Useful for a tool or a test that wants to check what a label is bound to.

gotchas.title: It writes to a text component on its OWN GameObject, not a child
gotchas.body: Auto-detection is GetComponent, not GetComponentInChildren — deliberately, so a panel full of labels cannot accidentally all bind to the first one. On a Button, put this on the Label child.

gotchas.title: An empty key is silent
gotchas.body: No key means no work and no warning, so a label you forgot to fill in looks identical to one that is working. Use the inspector preview to check: it shows the text in every language, and warns when a key resolves nowhere.

gotchas.title: Arguments live on the component, not in the key
gotchas.body: Two labels showing the same key can hold different arguments. Equally, a label whose key has no placeholders ignores its arguments entirely rather than erroring.
